subject: Big Healthcare Circles The Wagons As DHS Floats New H-1B Fee
posts:
Major medical associations push back against proposed Department of Homeland Security H-1B visa fees.
Evidence: AHA letters, AMA opposition, Regulatory lobbying
#Aletheia #Healthcare #Policy

Proposed H-1B fees target administrative abuse without harming essential medical staffing.
Stated Judgement: (1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Healthcare lobbies mobilize to protect institutional bottom lines under the pretext of patient access.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Institutional self-preservation masquerades as healthcare advocacy against regulatory fees.

Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.8, z: 3)

- American Hospital Association: FAIL (-0.6, -0.7) — Lobbies to exempt institutional labor costs.
- Department of Homeland Security: COND (-0.3, -0.4) — Imposes blunt fees with broad impacts.
The Department of Homeland Security's proposed H-1B visa fee hike has sparked fierce pushback from major medical associations warning of staffing shortages.

The Poison:
Institutional lobbies weaponize genuine patient care concerns to shield themselves from regulatory costs.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing institutional labor cost protection (WHO) with broad patient welfare principles (WHAT).

Social Physics Analysis:
Big Healthcare associations run a smart selfish maneuver, deploying public health pretexts to deflect financial burdens while projecting benevolence.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated altruism and institutional lobbying, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Defensive lobbying entrenches systemic costs.

The Unavoidable Truth: Large healthcare institutions fiercely protect their labor pipelines against regulatory cost increases.

The Unavoidable Lie: Industry opposition to visa fees is driven exclusively by selfless dedication to patient care.

Alethekanon:
Institutional self-interest wrapped in the sacred banner of patient welfare is a classic lobbying reflex.

Awwthekanon:
We all want doctors to be available, but institutions must also be transparent about their financial priorities.

Brothekanon:
Big hospitals yelling about visa fees because it hits their bottom line. Tale as old as time.

Spirithekanon:
"Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed" Isaiah 10:1 — FAIL (Justice Vector)
When powerful institutions lobby purely to protect their own privileges, true justice for the vulnerable is sidelined.

Big Healthcare Circles The Wagons As DHS Floats New H-1B Fee

‘make healthcare professionals exempt from any additional fees’

Actual Article Body:
(Photo by Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

Some of America’s biggest healthcare associations released letters of public comment condemning the Department of Homeland Security’s proposed H-1B visa regulation fees.

The window for submitting public comment regarding DHS’ proposed rule, “Fee for Certain H-1B Petition,” closed Thursday. The American Hospital Association (AHA) and American Medical Association (AMA) were two of several healthcare professional trade unions to criticize the $103,265 visa fee proposed by the Trump administration’s DHS.

In an open letter to Joseph Edlow, the Director of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), the AHA said that the new rule could significantly impact the doctors employed in the 5,000 hospitals it represents.

“The AHA recommends that DHS make healthcare professionals exempt from any additional fees to ensure continued access to timely, high-quality care for all communities,” the letter reads.
